newsitem.title: UK: UK's MAM unhappy with Granada bid price - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK's MAM unhappy with Granada bid price - paper.

text.p: Fund management group Mercury Asset Management is unhappy with the 11.75 stg bid at which Yorkshire Tyne-Tees board is negotiating to sell itself to media to hotels company Granada Group Plc, the Daily Telegraph reported.

The newspaper said in its Thursday edition that the fund manager had bought 100,000 shares in Yorkshire at 11.65 stg on Tuesday, taking its stake to just over five percent. MAM also holds a stake in Granada.

But the newspaper added: "It is not clear, however, if MAM is prepared to vote against the deal at 11.75 stg. It is thought to be waiting for a reaction from United News & Media, which owns 14 percent of Yorkshire."
Granada's chairman Gerry Robinson on Wednesday confirmed that the company was in talks with Yorkshire and that a price of 11.75 stg had been agreed.
Granada is seeking to buy the 73 percent of Yorkshire it does not already own.
